record.original_question: Is every 3-colourable planar graph representable by intersecting line segments that use only three slopes?

evidence.quote: Question 8.6 Is every 3-colourable planar graph representable by intersecting line segments with three different slopes?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A line-segment intersection representation of a graph $G=(V,E)$ assigns to each vertex $v\in V$ a closed line segment $S_v$ in the Euclidean plane such that, for any two distinct vertices $u,v$, the segments $S_u$ and $S_v$ intersect if and only if $uv\in E$. The representation is said to use $k$ slopes if every segment $S_v$ is parallel to one of $k$ fixed directions in the plane. A graph is 3-colourable if its vertices can be partitioned into three independent sets.

Question: Does every 3-colourable planar graph admit a line-segment intersection representation in the Euclidean plane using only three distinct slopes?
artifact.category_tag: geometric intersection representations of planar graphs
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (originally due to Scheinerman) has been resolved affirmatively. A proof by Castelli Aleardi, Gonçalves, and Ochem shows that every 3-colourable planar graph admits an intersection segment representation using only 3 slopes, appearing at WG 2019 and in an extended version on arXiv (2511.20368).

status_evidence.title: 3-colorable planar graphs have an intersection segment representation using 3 slopes
status_evidence.snippet: We prove that every 3-colorable planar graph has an intersection segment representation using only 3 slopes.

status_evidence.title: 3-Colorable Planar Graphs Have an Intersection Segment Representation Using 3 Slopes (WG 2019)
status_evidence.snippet: Conference proof that 3-colorable planar graphs have a 3-slope segment intersection representation.
